# APIs and services

Applies when the change touches: HTTP, gRPC, events, webhooks. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAPI or AsyncAPI contract | 3.2.1 (published 2026-09-10); 3.1.2 (2025-09-19) is the widest-toolchain baseline; events use AsyncAPI 3.1.0 (2026-01-31) | 2026-09-28 | <https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html> |
| RFC 9457 problem details | 2023 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457> |
| OWASP API Security Top 10 | 2023, second edition | 2026-09-28 | <https://api-security.owasp.org/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10/> |
| Idempotency keys and rate limits (emerging) | IETF httpapi drafts for idempotency-key and ratelimit headers | 2026-09-28 | <https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header/> |
| Semantic Versioning for public APIs | 2.0.0 | 2026-09-28 | <https://semver.org/> |
| Integration patterns: channel, endpoint, and the error-handling pattern each boundary uses | Hohpe and Woolf (2003); site current | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | A changed request, response, status code, or event is a contract change: never minor. |
| Specify | The OpenAPI or AsyncAPI change is written before Spec approval and listed in `design.files`, so Spec approval freezes it; the Acceptance references its operations and schemas. |
| Specify | Errors follow RFC 9457 problem details; every write has an idempotency strategy; rate limits are stated. |
| Implement | Validate input against the contract at the boundary; authorize per object and per property (OWASP API1, API3); paginate every list. |
| Review | Only additive changes without a version bump; removals go through expand and contract. |
| Ship | Consumer contract tests pass for every known consumer before rollout; 4xx and 5xx rates and p95 latency are the observe signals. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spectral | the OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document lints clean against the team ruleset | `spectral lint` in the test commands |
| Contract tests | every known consumer still passes against the head | Pact provider verification against every consumer contract, then `can-i-deploy` |
| Schema conformance | the running API matches its contract | Schemathesis against the running service |
| Breaking-change diff | no breaking change without a major version | `oasdiff breaking` between base and head documents |
| OWASP ZAP API scan | no high finding on the changed operations | `zap-api-scan.py` against a test deployment |
| Load test | the SLO holds under expected load | `k6 run` with thresholds |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
